newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-RUGBY UNION-One-off crack at Boks eases mental strain.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-RUGBY UNION-One-off crack at Boks eases mental strain.

text.p: WELLINGTON, July 7 - Mentally it will be easier than last year. Physically, just as tough.
That's the assessment from All Black centre Frank Bunce of the task awaiting the All Blacks at Ellis Park in Johannesburg on July 19.

Bunce, a happy man after his strong effort in Saturday's 30-13 Bledisloe Cup win over Australia in Christchurch, suggests the four consecutive tests against the Springboks last year became a grind that wore the All Blacks down.
They ultimately lost the last test, at Ellis Park. This time it's a one-off match, and Bunce believes that alone will make New Zealand's task easier.
"It became quite telling last year, when you know that you had to play the same team and that they would be just as hard as they were last time," Bunce said.
"It became an ongoing thing, but this time there's just the one game, you get there and prepare and bang. You do it and get out of there."
Bunce said the South Africans and Australians were equally difficult "but in different ways".
"That's going to be a hell of an afternoon up in Jo'burg. But these -- against the Wallabies and the Boks -- are the games you play rugby for, the big ones."
